## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** with a `<base>-touchpad` / `<base>-mouse` pair present, `off` disables both nodes and persists both names, reload re-disables both, and `on` re-enables both and clears the file. Devices without a sibling, touchscreens, `-touchpad-1` style names and names containing quotes or backslashes behave as before. The three new tests pass on this head and fail on the base commit, and each code change is caught by its own test. Hyprland v0.56.2 source confirms that touchpads and the emulation node are both listed under `mice`, and that a disabled pointer stays listed, so `on` can find the sibling again.

Two points are worth a look: the name match can also catch a pointing stick, and `on` does not re-enable the names that `off` saved.

### The `<base>-mouse` match can also disable a pointing stick

The kernel's HID input code puts a multitouch controller's mouse-type collections into one node named `<HID name> Mouse`. On I2C touchpad plus pointing-stick controllers, the stick reports through a mouse collection too. Upstream commit [40d5bb87377a](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/40d5bb87377a599d0405af765290f28aaa6abb1e) describes such controllers, with an emulation collection plus a separate trackstick collection that end up merged into one node. libinput also ships a Dell Latitude 7490 quirk that matches a `*Mouse` node as a pointing stick (`quirks/50-system-dell.quirks`).

```text
touchpad off on a touchpad + pointing-stick laptop (source-derived, not run on hardware)

<base>-touchpad   disabled        (intended)
<base>-mouse      disabled        (stick events can arrive here)
                  persisted  ->   re-disabled on every reload until "on"
```

Devices with the kernel quirk `MT_QUIRK_FORCE_MULTI_INPUT` get their nodes split without the ` Mouse` suffix, so this match does not select them. Which exact models expose a live stick in the `<base>-mouse` node was not confirmed on hardware.

**Impact:** on an affected laptop, turning the touchpad off also turns off the pointing stick and keeps it off across reloads. The base commit never touched this node.

**Suggested change:** limit the sibling toggle to devices where the `-mouse` node is known to be emulation only, or provide an opt-out, or at least document the pointing-stick case. udev's pointing-stick tag cannot tell the two apart here: current systemd hwdb sets it to 0 for I2C `*Mouse` nodes.

### `on` rediscovers the sibling instead of using the saved names

`enable()` removes the saved name file first, then runs a fresh `hyprctl devices -j` lookup. Two stubbed runs show the sibling that `off` disabled never receives `enabled = true`:

| Condition at `on` | Names re-enabled |
|---|---|
| Normal lookup | touchpad, `-mouse` |
| `hyprctl devices -j` fails once | touchpad only |
| `omarchy-hw-touchpad` now returns another device | the new device only |

Per Hyprland v0.56.2 source, a config reload clears `hl.device` entries and `setPointerConfigs` only re-attaches pointers that still have a device config. A missed sibling therefore stays disabled until Hyprland restarts or the device is re-added.

**Impact:** rare trigger conditions. The effect is invisible for a silent emulation node, but it leaves a pointing stick stuck off in the case above.

**Suggested change:** read the saved names before deleting the file and enable them together with the freshly detected names, mirroring what reload does.

**Related behavior:** a failed or empty second `hyprctl devices -j` call during `off` also falls back to disabling and saving only the touchpad, with a success exit status and OSD message. Separately, `on` sends `enabled = true` to a `-mouse` node even if the user had disabled it in their own config.

**Documentation note:** the header comments in `bin/omarchy-toggle-input-device` and `default/hypr/disabled-input-device.lua` still describe a single saved device name.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR, its callers and the reload path, plus Hyprland v0.56.2, Linux HID (`hid-input.c`, `hid-multitouch.c`), libinput quirks and systemd `input_id`/hwdb sources. Isolated, stubbed runs of the repository test script on head, base and hybrid trees, plus targeted behavior probes and a reload through the real `bootstrap.lua` and `toggles.lua` with a private home and state directory. No live compositor or input hardware was used. Whether pairing the two nodes fixes the reported finger-count desync was not verified on hardware; a run of this branch on the affected touchpad through many toggle cycles would settle it.
